critical_steps: The original three-vector family is Parseval, so its synthesis operator has norm one.
Every V_c in the displayed family satisfies T_Lambda V_c = K.
V_c^* V_c is diagonal with entries one and one-quarter plus c squared.
Every dual has norm at least one, while all |c| <= sqrt(3)/2 attain one.
Only c=0 satisfies the Douglas reduced-range condition.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact finite-dimensional synthesis and analysis matrices.
integrity.unproved_limits: No claim is made that the reduced-range condition is the only possible convention for defining a canonical dual.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects the uniqueness clause of Proposition 3.7, not the existence of a minimum-norm controlled dual.
The example concerns operator-norm minimality; stricter pointwise coefficient-minimality criteria are not assessed.
A nonindexed erratum or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: Minimal operator norm does not uniquely determine a canonical controlled \(K\)-\(g\)-dual
